utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. We would like briefly to deal with a matter in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Adamovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We had a few matters to deal with prior to commencing your evidence again. I'm sorry we kept you waiting, but your

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you gave at the outset continues to apply to your evidence today. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Adamovic.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Have you had a bit of a rest? I have a few questions for you and I will start with paragraph 8 of your statement. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me take a look.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all microphones please be switched off except for the speaker's. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in paragraph 8 you were explaining the appointment of Radoslav Djinovic. According to this decision, as far as I can see, he was appointed deputy head of staff of the MUP for the area of Kosovo. Is there a decision appointing you assistant head of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it, but there must have been one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, according to that decision and by the very nature of these activities, what was your exact duty in the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can say that it was police work. That is what it would really correspond to, what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What was your exact job description, what was your job called?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the decision on my appointment. As far as I can remember it arrived after I got to Pristina. Now, was it for operative work, police work, is that what it read? I cannot say with any degree of certainty but it certainly should be in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that perhaps it could be assistant head of the staff for interventions and operative planning?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree. It's certainly not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you define your job more specifically because in this decision on the establishment of the staff I see that every assistant head has his activity exactly set out. 1505 is the number, P1505. Can we please see this document, P1505, on our screens.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 28 I said briefly what it was that I dealt with, paragraph in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that my question was very specific, but I see in this document, for instance, the assistant head for special operations, for police, et cetera. I'm interested in your exact duty. What was it specifically?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we look at these decisions on appointment, during my preparations I saw a few. As far as the members of the staff are concerned, obviously the ministry did not do this in a uniform manner as regards the job descriptions of the members of the staff, what it was that they were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether you can tell me specifically what this was or not. If you can't, let's move on. Just one sentence, one word, assistant head of staff --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant head of staff, what I did primarily related to logistics, what I did, if that is what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Adamovic, who you replaced from this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who it was that I replaced. I arrived on the 5th of July, 1998, and I did not find anyone who would hand this duty over to me and instruct me in terms of the work that he had been doing until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you possibly consider yourself to be number two in the staff under General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I could not consider myself number two because I know who number two was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Maybe I will clarify with the next document. Could we have P1071, please. Could we have second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you seen the first page, Mr. Adamovic, have you seen the first page?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now, the bottom -- on the bottom of the page - could we please see it in English as well - we have the call-signs for radio link users for the MUP staff. Tell me, in terms of the numbers we see here what Kosava number would you be?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know because I did not use these communications systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So how was it that you communicated with the commanders of the PJP units?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the commanders of the units I communicated if they would call from the field or if they would stop by the staff because they were not duty-bound to call me and I wasn't duty-bound to call them either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What equipment did you use for communication?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Telephone links most of the time if they called the staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask my colleague to specify time, before the war, summer, wartime, because this was unit was different over different times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Specifically I'm referring to the summer of 1998, Mr. Adamovic. All these questions pertain to that period because I know that later you were injured and that you were recovering through most of the war. So in the summer of 1998 when anti-terrorist actions took place, am I right if I say that you were using Motorolas radio communication in order to communicate from time to time with the officers from the PJP units?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not communicate with them in that way or was there any need for me to communicate in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Up until the 28th, or rather, the 29th of March, 1999, you carried out your duties at the staff. Am I right if I say that Lieutenant-Colonel Arsenijevic replaced you in those duties?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that Lieutenant-Colonel Arsenijevic is also a graduate of the military academy?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have on our screens 6D773 on the right-hand side and on the left-hand side 5D1418, the last page. Thank you. I need both documents in B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, if we look at this document on the right-hand side of the screen, 150 are the last numbers that are printed there, Colonel Mijatovic confirmed to me that the signature down here was his, Colonel Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My colleague asked Colonel Zivaljevic and Colonel Zivaljevic allowed for the possibility that this is Arsenijevic's signature. We see that signature and we see it on this document. You will agree with me that this is actually Lieutenant-Colonel Arsenijevic's signature?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how he signs his name, but it says Arsa or something like that. You can see A-r-s, that is quite obvious. I assume that it's him, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Adamovic, your statement is in front of you and can we have a look at paragraph 17. You claim here that the staff was not involved in any way in the planning or organization or direction of anti-terrorist operations. Even if it had been envisaged that the staff should plan anti-terrorist actions this was rendered invalid by the adoption of the plan to fight terrorism which was drawn up at the level of the state, and so on and so forth. Are you saying that in this way the document dated June 1998, P1505, became invalid, therefore?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that the staff no longer existed because we were still down there, but what we did is a well-known thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was this decision that I quoted a few moments ago still in force?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I did not see another one. During the operations here I saw these decisions. Whether there was some other one, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what are you saying that planning anti-terrorist activity was -- became invalid, was suspended?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is an assertion in relation to what the staff did. I know what the staff did, and I'm just saying that by way of an assertion that the staff did not plan anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll look at minutes from a staff meeting, P3121 is what I'd like to have displayed now. This is a record of the staff meeting dated the 29th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next page, please. Another page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, you attended this meeting. We can see that here, it's stated in the introductory part.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just see the bottom of the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at these words. General Lukic is speaking, it's the sixth line from the end. It says: "The second stage of the global plan was carried out."

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you read that.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The second stage of the global plan has been carried out in accordance with the established schedule with ten detachments. Actions were carried out in coordination with the Army of Yugoslavia (he gave a detailed explanation about the locations at which actions had been carried out and what had been achieved showing axes of action and other things on a topographic map). He stressed that the next task was to liberate and capture Drenica."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this is seven days after the 22nd of July, and you said that any kind of staff planning was derogated then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the following page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, you understood what was meant by the global plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's a plan that was explained to us, disclosed to us, in a meeting. It was said that a plan had been adopted for carrying out anti-terrorist actions in whose implementation the army and police were to participate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see that ten detachments have been mentioned, ten police detachments. Can you tell me, please, what kind of designations did they have, single-digit or two-digit designations in that summer?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to detachment designations, they had their own designations, if I may call them that, when they were in the territory of Serbia proper before coming to Kosovo. However, once they came to Kosovo during the preparations for carrying out actions in contact with the Pristina Corps, these figures were reformulated so that from then on we had both single-digit and two-digit designations but we always knew exactly which detachments those were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, in this courtroom we saw a document sending the forces to the territory of Kosmet where designations of detachments are clearly indicated on the 21st or 22nd of March, and it says there from the 21st to 87th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And this document was signed at the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And there is no mention of the army whatsoever, no mention of the army either specifying these numbers or sending the forces?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document there can only be numerical designations that the detachments had, and this is how these units were recognised in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who identified or who set those designations?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Djakovic when I provided the information. I don't know why this was reformulated into numbers 1 to 10, but I know that both myself and Colonel Djakovic knew exactly what that meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is there a decision on setting these designations, numbers of detachments?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the Pristina Corps creating a plan for carrying out actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you look at page 2 of this document. Would you look at the top of the page and read the last sentence in the first paragraph where it says: "We need at least 2.000 more policemen ..." Would you please read out that sentence.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We need at least another 2.000 policemen, especially if possible volunteers from the reserve police forces. Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic says this is a correction of the main plan."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Read the next sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Major-General Sreten Lukic responded with a yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Adamovic, do you stand by the position that after the 22nd of June, 1998, the Main Staff -- the 22nd of July, 1998, the Main Staff did not plan, organize, prepare any anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to anti-terrorist actions in which --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please give us brief answers. Yes or no, do you stand by your position presented in the statement or not? Just give us a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see your name at the bottom, and here you mention ammunition for 82-, 60-, and 120-millimetre mortars. Did all detachments have all three types of mortars?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't think so. I don't think they did. 82 and 60, yes, they had that, but not 120.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: At one of the meetings at the staff Colonel Zivaljevic pointed out the problem of lacking ammunition for 20- and 30-millimetre calibre weapons, for PATs, which is anti-aircraft gun. What kind of ammunition is that, for what kind of a weapon?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an acronym, and since I didn't study this at the academy I think it stands for anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that this 20-millimetre ammunition that Colonel Zivaljevic requested is the ammunition for anti-aircraft guns on armoured vehicles known as BOV and BVP which were part of his brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what he needed the ammunition for since I didn't go out in the field and I wasn't fully familiar with what kind of weapons of that nature existed in the units. However, it is certain that before the arrival the police did not have such equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why is he then asking for ammunition, Colonel Zivaljevic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said before arrival in Kosovo, before arriving in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, won't you, that within 122nd and 124th Intervention Brigades in the territory of Kosovo there existed armoured vehicles known as BOV and BVP?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armoured vehicles existed within the establishment units of the police from a previous period of time. They were used as armoured vehicles intended for transporting policemen from one location to another location in case where they could come under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And in those tasks these brigades, 122nd and 124th, were the prominent ones, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although the 122nd one had very few, I don't know exactly how many, but very few pieces of such equipment, they were quite old and basically almost could not be used anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The 124th had many more armoured pieces of equipment, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had more.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel Zivaljevic also mentioned 30-millimetre ammunition, saying that he needed that as well. You will agree with me, won't you, that the 30-millimetre ammunition is needed for Praga; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know what Praga looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, you say that you don't even know what Praga looks like, and you completed military academy. You have just told us that you dealt with logistics and now I'm all confused.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These pieces of equipment were not routinely used by police units. I did graduate from the military academy, but I don't remember encountering such equipment while at the academy. I don't think we even studied that equipment within the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, at this meeting your words are quoted here. Would you please look at this. It says here: "Wheel sets for armoured vehicles," you mentioned BOV vehicles and then you say that you don't know what these types of equipment looked like.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: BOV and Praga are two different things. Here at the meeting I'm mentioning the requests that had come from the field. It's not like I was out in the field requesting this equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So you can still discern between a BOV and a Praga?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since I know what a BOV is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's questionable whether I would be able to recognise a BOV because there are several model -- several types of these armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We had a question here dealing with command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the last page of this document, please. It's on the screens in front of us. We need the words uttered by Minister Stojiljkovic. Fifth line from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please read that sentence.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Commanding is better."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Adamovic. Now, let's look at a brief video excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Defence Exhibit 5D1455, which is a videotape dating 10th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "A visit was organized today for foreign journalists accredited in Belgrade to the places that have recently been subjected to increased activity by Siptar terrorist gangs" --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately we have some technical problem and we hope that my assistant will solve that in a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "In Belgrade a visit was organized today for foreign journalists accredited to the places that have recently been subjected to increased activity by Siptar terrorist acts. Police General Sreten Lukic and the chief of the State Security Service for Kosovo and Metohija, David Gajic, briefed the reporters on the current situation in the territory of Decani municipality, which has recently been particularly subjected to terrorist attacks. Gajic said that the terrorists' objective was to take full control of the area, cleanse it ethnically, and thus make it possible for terrorist gangs from Albania to infiltrate and bring in weapons. The terrorists' targets in the attacks were houses of Serbs and Montenegrins, but also those owned by Albanians loyal to Serbia. The foreign journalists particularly wanted to know about Serbian and Montenegrin civilian casualties. "The terrorists have committed a series of crimes against the Serbian population. 73 Serbian families have been moved out without the right to take anything from their houses with them. 200 Serbs and Montenegrins who wanted to return from Montenegro were not allowed to do so. During this short period of time, eight Serbs were killed, eight were abducted and their whereabouts remain unknown and eight people were wounded. During this period there were also several attacks on convoys and police patrols that were bringing food to refugees and civilians. "About 70 foreign journalists visited Decani, Crnobreg, and Prilep to see firsthand what the objectives of the renegade terrorist gangs made up of members of the Albanian ethnic minority were. The attacks from these locations, real bunkers were synchronised, General Lukic stressed, and the journalists could see it for themselves, that only the houses from which Siptar terrorists had fired on the police and civilians were damaged during the operation."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, we have just seen this video excerpt dated 10th of June, 1998, and this is a report on legitimate anti-terrorist actions in the territory of Decani municipality as carried out by police forces, and in this excerpt we saw General Lukic explaining on the map the movement of units --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. I haven't seen General Lukic showing movement of the units on the map, I haven't seen it, maybe somebody else saw it in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the footage was clear enough. If necessary, we can show it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can ask the witness what he saw General Lukic doing and you can proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I saw General Lukic standing in front --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, we'll ask the witness, Mr. Lukic, please, rather than prompting, as has caused us a great deal of concern with the objections. The objection is legitimate but not the supplementary --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that the witness has now been suggested what his answer should be, but nevertheless I will put my question to him. Mr. Adamovic, what kind of the map could we see behind General Lukic and generally what kind of maps existed in the map on which General Lukic showed the movement of units as we can see in the document that we just read dated the 29th --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection, has it been establish that this is a meeting of the MUP staff, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what this relates to is a visit for foreign journalists, and somewhere or other I've got the date the 10th of June, 1998. Now, the location, I'm not sure about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave I would now ask the witness about the video footage that we have seen, but I see that Mr. Hannis is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I do have an objection regarding foundation, Your Honour. The 10th of June, 1998, is the date I think we heard from Mr. Cepic, not from the witness. This witness, as I understand, did not come to Kosovo until July of 1998. So I'm not sure whether he can assist us with this at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, no. What's your response to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a very brief period of time, only 20 days, and the witness probably knows about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On what basis?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Membership on the staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But he wasn't there on the 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly later on in July he had knowledge of the actions carried out by the MUP in June in the area of Decani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if that's your question I don't know what we were looking at a video for. Let's hear what your question is and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, has be established whether Sreten Lukic was member of the MUP staff at that time also. It has to be established the location, many things, before something is proposed to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's hear what the question is, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, I assume that you had knowledge about independent police actions that were carried out in the month of June just before you arrived in Kosmet, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had knowledge only of the complex situation, if I can put it that way, and on the intensified activity of the Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On this video footage we saw a map, a topographic map. What kind of maps did you use in the staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Geography maps for the most part and topographic maps of the area of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who drew the axes of movement of MUP units for independent MUP actions on these maps?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of whether this was drawn and whether they had topographic maps out in the field. The police practically does not have topographic maps in its regular work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, let's not go back to the document. On the 29th of July, the meeting, General Lukic indicated on a topographic map the axes of activity of the PJP detachments. Who drew the axes of PJP activity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just before you answer that. Mr. Lukic has already objected to the formulation of that question, but his objection is to the part that is narrative which any of us can assess for ourselves. Your question is simply: Who drew the axes of PJP activity. Now, how do you expect this witness to know that when he wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked him now about the meeting on the 29th of July, 1998, in the wish to save time so that we don't open yet again the document that we looked at a few moments ago but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought we were looking at the same material, so it's my mistake. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have to doubt, Mr. Cepic, what the point of that video was now in showing it and --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I expected the witness to provide more information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you should focus your cross-examination and finish it by the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, we saw at this meeting that you attended on the 29th of July that General Lukic gave more detailed explanation on a topographic map regarding the axes of activity of the PJP. Who was it that drew these axes on the map for the independent actions of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the axes of activity were not drawn on that map and they were not on that map in the first place. This was purely a topographic map on which General Lukic indicated with his own hand what the axes were. So it was not a map that had been drawn on. These were anti-terrorist actions that were already underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who drew maps for the detachments themselves for their independent actions?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one from the staff drew maps for the detachments. I don't even know to which extent the detachments took part in these independent actions. They don't really --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that the detachments did not take part in independent actions?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just explain so that it's clearer to all?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You've just said that.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we talk about anti-terrorist actions --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you specifically, Mr. Adamovic. Please let us move through my questions faster. I'm putting them very simply and I'm saying in terms of independent actions of PJP detachments, who drew their maps for them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It first has to be established whether there were independent actions of MUP detachments, and time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why don't you give an example, Mr. Cepic --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- that might assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With your leave, I will start with another topic and I will catch also this one. [Interpretation] P1991, could we have that on our screens, please, and 1990 as well, please. So -- actually, I made a mistake. I'm asking for 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, the 17th of February, 1999, meeting at the MUP staff. You attended that meeting, didn't you? It says here all members of the staff.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the answer is probably yes then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the bottom of the first page. A plan was elaborated. Could you please read that sentence out to me.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A plan of the RJB was elaborated in order to prevent and thwart entry of NATO troops into our territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Next sentence.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The staff planned to carry out, when so ordered, three actions of cleansing the area of terrorists in the Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica areas and police forces were prepared for that of around 4.000 policemen" --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Fine. That will do. What does RJB mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5D1428, could we have that on our screens now, please. Unfortunately we don't have a translation of this document, so could we please have a look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, we don't have a translation of this document, so could you please read the header.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Republic of Serbia, the Ministry of the Interior, staff of the ministry, 12A number, the 25th of January, 1999, Pristina."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And what is the heading, what does the title say?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Information on the activities of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia in combatting terrorism in the area of Kosovo and Metohija in the period from the 27th of October, 1998, until the 25th of January, 1999."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 5 on e-court now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, we don't have a translation of this document, so could you please read the fourth paragraph from the top.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In addition to increased engagement of the police in the implementation of all tasks, several planned actions were carried out involving a larger number of participants (the 15th, 16th, and 17th of December in Kapasnica and other neighbourhoods in Pec; on the 14th of December in Donja Lapastica; on the 17th of December in Glodjane; on the 25th and 26th of December in the neighbourhoods of Bajir and Tamnik in Kosovska Mitrovica; on the 27th of December in Obrandza; on the 9th of January in Perani; on the 14th through the 16th of January in the area of the village of Dasinovac; on the 15th and 17th --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please try and focus this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Adamovic, you will agree with me that several independent police actions were enumerated here with the dates of their implementation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who drew the maps for the implementation of these independent actions by the MUP, a few were enumerated here right now.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot say whether any were drawn and if so by who. Obviously this has to do with police actions that had been planned by the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying, Mr. Adamovic, that in your experience you have never seen a map relating to an action that was prepared by a member of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I claim that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the meeting of the 17th of February we saw that there was a plan of the RJB. Could you please read out the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The next paragraph, it starts with the words: "With a view to the more efficient ..."

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "With a view to the more efficient implementation of tasks an action plan was drawn up in case NATO tries to enter the territory of Kosovo and Metohija from Macedonia in a violent manner. This plan was submitted to all secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija and to border police stations in order for them to become familiar with it."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many days is this before the 17th of February, this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what the day was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The 25th of January, the 25th of January, that's what the heading said.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How many days is this before that meeting that was held on the 17th of February?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my math is right, it's 22 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It's excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at 6D716 again, please. Could we please call up 6D716 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, you gave your comments in respect of this document in your statement. Do you have it before you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This order of the MUP command dated the 19th of February, 1999, who does it issue orders to, tasks to who, only the Ministry of the Interior --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: MUP command. We have had testimony from other witnesses that there is no such a body. Yesterday we showed that this document has never been produced inside the MUP. It first has to be established what kind of document, then proposing that there is some kind of MUP command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's a matter for us to consider in due course. We're looking at the moment at a document which clearly makes -- refers to MUP command and questions about it are perfectly legitimate and we'll decide in due course what weight if any to give the document and the answers that are given to questions relating to it. So we repel that objection. Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, may I call you Colonel, do you mind?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Are you a colonel or a general, you were retired with what rank?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General would have been a nicer rank, do you think you think, but I'm going to address you as colonel.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that in paragraph 5 tasks are issued only to the units of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Tasks are issued to the units of the ministry as well as to the units of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If you say so.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document says so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why don't you turn to page 4, page 4 in e-court, item 5, 5.1, please. Let us now see, this is Zivaljevic's unit. Doesn't it say here that this is the task only for the 22nd Detachment of PJP?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it says with the support of BG 211th and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But the task is issued exclusively to the 22nd Detachment; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why don't you read this out, tell us what it says there. Please start with 5.1. It says here: "22nd Detachment of PJP without the 5th and the 6th" --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "The 22nd Detachment of the PJP without the 5th and 6th Company of the PJP ... from the deployment sector to be brought to the following line: Donja Repa, Prepolac, village of Donja Lopastica. Still no task and then the task. Starting from a semiflexible position along the Krpimej village - Prepolac - Donja Lopastica village, Obrandza village, and with the support by BG 211 carry out a comprehensive attack along the axes" -- should I read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No. Why don't you read 5.2 to us, item 5.2.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "5th Detachment of the PJP from the deployment sector to be brought to the following line: Glavnik village - Sibovac village. "Task: With the support of BG 15-1, carry out attack along the following axis."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why don't you read item 5.4 to us, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The SAJ to be sent from their deployment sector to the sector of Gornja Pak astica village and Kraljevci village. "Task: During the night the unit shall on D-1 get into the broader sector of Kodralija village, Rekalija village, Krs trig point 1103, and shall prevent the withdrawal of Siptar terrorist forces from the areas of Bradas village, Bajcina village, Dobroin village, and then withdrawing to the sector of Bajgora."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. We don't need to read all of it. It's all part of the evidence now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's part of the evidence anyway by you drawing attention to it but you haven't asked a question. Mr. Adamovic, are you actually saying that in 5.1 and 5.2 there are tasks issued to anybody other than the PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One can see there that there are also tasks given to some other forces; however, this order as a whole looks suspicious or questionable to me and I can explain if needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not what you're being asked. You're being asked whether it bears to issue tasks to any forces other than the PJP. Now, what's the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there are tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, that's interesting because there are many more VJ documents written in similar language referring to the MUP and to other bodies such as the armed non-Siptar population, so your evidence will assist us in interpreting these. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, have you graduated from the military academy?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you read orders, are you able to?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a soldier in the true sense of the word. I graduated from the military academy 18 years before the events in Kosovo. It is possible that I do not have the best observation when it comes to certain issues. These are my interpretations. Now, as to whether they are correct or not I can't tell you because I haven't dealt with these issues for 18 years. I just told you about what I read in the documents, what the documents say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the 22nd PJP Detachment could not command a combat group of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat once again. The 22nd Detachment cannot be expected to command a combat group; however, if all of this pertains to an anti-terrorist action where broader forces are participating then it is the Pristina Corps that draws up plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, I'm not asking you who draws up a plan. I just asked you to read out what it says here. You read this out and you gave a completely different interpretation, unlike all other witnesses who came here.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is possible that I'm just ignorant when it comes to these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us please look at item 866, the last page in the B/C/S version, I suppose it's the same in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Item 866, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: 8.6.6, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, on this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, precisely, Your Honour. Thank you. Could we have the last page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Adamovic, who was at the head of the PJP command in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The PJP command was not engaged at all in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And who was supposed to be there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should have been both the commander and the command if it was operational at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document is from the 19th of February?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we now look at P1990, which are the minutes of the meeting on the 17th of February. The meeting was held two days before this document was drafted, the document that we just looked at, Mr. Adamovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You read the bottom part and I will ask you to read that again and also the following sentence in its entirety. Could we now see the bottom part, please. Please look -- start reading from the following sentence: "The staff planned ..."

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... once it was ordered to carry out three operations cleansing the terrain from the terrorists in the Podujevo" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just stop. What's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't want you reading things for the sake of having them in the transcript, and you've been tending to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With your leave, the next sentence is very important and I need the context of both sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could the witness continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Adamovic, could you please continue.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... in the sectors of Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica and the police forces numbering about 4.000 members, about 70 policemen from an OPG group, and about 900 police reservists were planned for that."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now the following sentence.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On Saturday, 20 February 1999, a meeting will be held at the staff with all commanders of police unit detachments for further consultations and their engagement."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, what's your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, we see that the day after this MUP staff order was issued a meeting was scheduled for all commanders of PJP detachments. Who chaired the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that meeting, I truly don't. That was nine years ago after all. Perhaps if you have a document that could refresh my memory about what was discussed then I could perhaps remember some things if this meeting was held at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps have an idea who should have chaired that meeting that was held in February of 1999?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depends on the topic. Looking at this it's hard to say. I would have to speculate; that's not something I would do gladly because I can't make conclusions on the basis of what is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All PJP commanders were invited?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but without a topic that was to be discussed at the meeting it would be hard for me to analyse it further.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You read out the previous sentence where it says that the staff planned three actions, and then the follow-up question is that a meeting was scheduled on the 20th of February?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what you have in mind, then the meeting was definitely not scheduled on that account because such meetings were not held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not following you. It says a meeting will be held. So what are you saying about that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm saying that I don't know whether the meeting was held and for what reason. The question put to me was whether this meeting pertained to the action mentioned in the document, and I know that we did not hold meetings with detachment commanders on account of this action or other similar actions. So, it is not quite clear what the topic of this meeting was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It says clearly what it was. It says that a plan's been worked out to prevent and thwart the entry of NATO troops, the staff plans when it is ordered to carry out three mopping-up operations using a large force of men that's described. On Saturday, 20th February, a meeting of the staff will be held with all police unit detachment commanders for further consultations and their engagement was the translation we got a moment ago. Are you saying that's a meeting about something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have simply no information. I just don't remember whether this meeting was held at all. We can see here that there was a meeting on the 17th of February and then this following was allegedly scheduled for the 20th. I simply don't remember whether it was held; and if so, what was discussed, what attended it, and so on. I simply don't have any recollections about it, not enough to be able to give any comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you've said something else. You've said that: "We did not hold meetings with detachment commanders on account of this action or any other action." So you a moment ago said you do remember that there was no such meeting. Now, which is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I apologise. Perhaps it was misinterpreted. I did not say that this meeting on the 20th of February was held. It says here that it is supposed to be held, but I simply don't remember whether it was held or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will ask CLSS to give us a revised translation of page 37, 5 to 11. Mr. Cepic, what else do you have to ask about?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: A couple of questions in relation to -- in relation to MUP staff and some document from 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you do that in ten minutes after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I will try to do my best, Your Honour, but this witness is so important it's very important so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We appreciate he's important, but we also feel that you've asked a number of things that really didn't focus the issues of importance. So it may emerge that we're wrong about that, of course, and that you have actually identified the ones that really matter. I -- we will be very reluctant to exceed another 15 minutes, Mr. Cepic. So please bring your mind to bear over the break and what you really need to ask in that time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We need to have a break at this stage, Mr. Adamovic, that will be for 20 minutes. So please again leave the courtroom with the usher. We'll see you again at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Adamovic, it's me again.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In your statement and during your testimony you mentioned that from the corps you were in contact with then-Colonel Djakovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Colonel Djakovic in the beginning of 1999 left the corps and went to another duty?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find it necessary to have contact with representatives of the Pristina Corps afterwards?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, I said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you something about reserve police stations or branches. Yesterday you said to my colleague Mr. Ackerman that RPO were armed by the MUP and by the Army of Yugoslavia. Am I right if I say that for its own needs the MUP temporarily engaged within the RPO military conscripts from the Army of Yugoslavia as well who had their own weapons that had been issued to them?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this was not exactly my line of work, as far as I know, in these RPOs there were reserve policemen and reserve soldiers too. How the actual arming took place I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said to my colleague Mr. Ackerman that your role in terms of implementing tasks within the MUP was a totally unimportant one and that you were not aware of the situation concerning the so-called KLA in the field, what their strength was, and so on. At meetings of the MUP staff was there any discussion about terrorist forces in the territory of Kosmet?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was information when the chiefs of secretariats were present and when they said what it was that was happening in their respective areas, but with that exception the staff never discussed these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: However, I assume that the staff did have information to the effect that the KLA was preparing a spring offensive?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certain that there was a link, if I can put it that way, in this kind of mutual exchange of information with the RDB, with the Pristina Corps, and so on; however, I did not take part in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That really isn't an answer to that question. I mean, did you have information that the KLA was preparing a spring offensive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This information, if I can put it that way, is something that we did receive and if we can put it this way, the head of the staff in a way transmitted this to us and also such information was coming in from the field that quite simply this spring offensive was being prepared for these -- and that these units were being additionally armed and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3122 is what I'd like to have called up now, please. Page 3, please, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, we see that you were present at that meeting as well. In all fairness, at that time it was Lieutenant-Colonel Dusko Adamovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's just look at the last page in B/C/S, or rather, the fourth one, the one-but-last in B/C/S. Could we please see the page before this in English. It's the second bullet point in English. Do you see at the top of the page in Serbian: "The Siptar terrorists are organizing and setting out in a decisive offensive in the spring ..." Do you remember these words?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that I remember these exact words now, but if that is what is recorded in the minutes then that was certainly discussed and that was certainly said. There is no reason for me to doubt, well, I've already said this, that we had this kind of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you talked about the global plan and the combat against terrorism, you actually meant the period from July to September 1998, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I talked about these things in general I was just referring to what it was that the police did and what it was that the police and army did. It is best perhaps to separate these two segments that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You meant the implementation of this plan in the July to September period, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen that plan so I don't know what period it referred to and what it said actually. It was said what it was that the police and the army were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. No further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, you'll now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Stamp -- sorry, my mistake. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No problem. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not wishful thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel. I'll start with asking you some questions --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- about your witness statement, Exhibit 6D1613. In paragraph 2 you tell us that you were assigned to Kosovo from the 5th of July, 1998, until the time that you were injured and left on the 29th of March, 1999. Can you tell us how you came to be assigned to Kosovo? How did you first find out about it? Did you receive a written document or did someone come in and tell you? How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My superior told me about that, my superior in the organizational unit that I worked in and that is the secretariat in Belgrade, the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan Maksimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember how many days that was before I was actually sent there, but it wasn't more than seven days before I was sent there, perhaps it was even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That seems like pretty short notice. Did he tell you why you were being picked for that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't tell me and I didn't ask. As a professional even until then I went out on different assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think you told us earlier that you don't have a copy of the document that made that assignment, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But did you see a copy of that document at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the document reached Pristina while I was already down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you see it then down there sometime in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I take it that's the only way we know that you were a member of the MUP staff was because it said so on that document?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what's written in the document, my document, my individual document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who signed that document, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, I think, it was signed by the chief of the public security sector, that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us in your statement in paragraph 6 about who the staff members were when you arrived on the 5th of July, 1998. Did you ever see a document naming all those people of -- as members of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it here during my preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You saw a document naming these people in item number 6, that is, Lukic, Mijatovic, Zdravkovic, et cetera, or --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw several documents here pertaining to the membership on the staff, and there are different persons mentioned in the documents I saw. So not all of these people are mentioned in one single document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's what I'm curious about. I -- we here have all seen Exhibit P1505 which is that 16 June 1998 document creating a MUP staff for the suppression of terrorism. Do you need to see that one again? Would it help you if I showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on what the question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, just for convenience let me give you a copy. I can hand you a hard copy. Now, you saw that one before, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this is one that's signed by Minister Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you see on there that the deputy head in this document is listed as David Gajic not Miroslav Mijatovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the document, but that's not the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you personally ever see a document that named Miroslav Mijatovic as deputy head of staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall having seen him -- well, only the decision, his decision, but I did not see him but I saw the decision referring to him personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that P1505 that's on the screen here?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No. That's -- that looks like the witness's statement that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you if you remember because you talked about seeing the -- your own decision that made you a member of the staff. Have you ever seen the document since that time? You don't have a copy of your own; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a copy of my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it's been confusing to some of us, or at least to me, because I've seen some other documents about a MUP staff in Kosovo and it's just basically called a ministerial staff in Kosovo. But this document, P1505, talks about a ministerial staff for the suppression of terrorism, a very specific name. And I just wondered, do you remember now what your personal appointment document said? Did it say you were a member of the MUP staff in Kosovo or did it say you were a member of the MUP staff for the suppression of terrorism or something else?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard for me to answer that question because I really do not remember. I think that usually the formulation was the MUP staff, but I'm not making any assertions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's perfectly understandable to me. It was a long time ago. What about the appointment document for Mr. Mijatovic, do you remember what it said?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember because I never saw his document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you in your preparation for testifying here did you see or did anyone show you a document creating a MUP staff in the end of May or the beginning of June 1999? Do you recall if you were shown that document?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen it. Maybe I did see it because there were many documents, but I don't remember, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Going back just briefly to the video-clip you viewed earlier, did you see David Gajic in that video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you see David Gajic in Kosovo after you arrived in July 1998 during the -- did you see him during that second half of the year in 1998 in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a while he was there but when he exactly returned I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned in paragraphs 7 through 9 Mr. Gajic, Legija, Zivko Trajkovic, Radoslav Djinovic, and Misa Vilotic, and in paragraph 10 of your statement you say you didn't hear from the colleagues who had come to the staff before you that those persons were ever involved in the work of the staff. But you didn't ask them about that, did you, you wouldn't have any reason to ask them if Gajic and Djinovic and those others ever did any work on the staff, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if I understood correctly you never saw this document, P1505, until you came here to prepare to testify; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And in paragraph 12 of your statement you mention that the head of staff wasn't authorised to appoint or dismiss members but that he could make recommendations. And you say that before candidates or staff members were selected consultations about this were held with each line of work at the MUP head office. Now, do you mean the consultations were held at the MUP headquarters in Belgrade about candidates for MUP staff in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the MUP command but in the MUP that is a regular thing, a usual thing. If an officer who has a particular line of work, now is it police, is it crime prevention or other jobs, it is only natural to have consultations within that administration. And it usually makes a proposal as to who it is that could do that particular job.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I mean, that sounds logical to me and I understand that's a good way to proceed, but how do you know that? Do you know personally that that was done in this situation in June of 1998 and July of 1998 when you were appointed?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot make any assertions specifically about this staff, but my experience from the previous period, because for a while I worked in the ministry, leads me to draw that conclusion. In this case I cannot confirm this fully but it's the usual thing, at least that's the way it was in the ministry while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to move to paragraph 16 where you say the staff was not involved in any way in the planning, organization, and leadership of the MUP organizational units in Kosovo and Metohija. My first question is: What was your understanding about the definition of that term "organizational units" in Kosovo? What would those have been?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to MUP organizational units, both in Kosovo and outside of Kosovo, there is a document within the ministry about organization, how the ministry 's organized, what its organizational units are. Secretariats of the interior were established in Kosovo, a total of seven of them, as organizational units of the ministry. The same principle was applied as in other parts of Serbia when it comes to the way the ministry was organized.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So in addition to SUPs were there any other organizational units in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean those that were sent there or the ones existing in Kosovo? There were border police stations outside of SUPs or in addition to SUPs, and they were directly linked to the -- to their administration within the seat of the ministry, which means they were not part of the Kosovo secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But were border police considered organizational units?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was an organizational unit, or rather, those were parts of the border police administration which existed within the ministry seat and they had stations that existed for controlling how the state border is crossed both in the territory of Kosovo and outside of Kosovo, and all of those units belonged to the border police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the border police administration was considered an organizational unit of the MUP, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What about the PJP?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when it comes to PJPs they were not organizational units. Why? In addition to the document on organization defining these units as I've described to you, there is also a document on how staffing requirements are resolved so that within each organizational unit jobs would be defined and number of people needed to perform those jobs. When it comes to PJPs, members of the police who were members of PJPs were organized or assigned to secretariats and they performed regular police duties. That is to say they were not a separate organizational unit. If needed, I can additionally explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you a question first and then maybe I'll ask you to do that. Then if I understand, isn't it correct that every individual who was a member of the PJP was also a member of some secretariat?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the secretariats were organizational units, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the ministry, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have Exhibit 1505 in front of you still, that MUP staff decision?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you would look at -- I'm not sure what page it is for you, I think it might be page 2, it's item number 2 right after the sentence about other members of the ministry may be appointed to the staff on request to the head. Do you see that item number 2? It says: "The staff is tasked with planning ..."

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at the decision that I have, the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, do you see item number 2: "The staff is tasked with planning, organizing, and managing the activities and use of the organizational units of the ministry, both the sent and attached units ..." Can you give me an example of a sent organizational unit in Kosovo in 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: PJP units can be considered as units that were sent, any one of them can be considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Right. But from what you answered before I understood that PJP weren't considered organizational units.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not considered that. I said that members of a PJP belonged to a secretariat, and a secretariat is an organizational unit of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The difference between organizational unit and unit, so maybe it causes confusion but it's -- those are two different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, my first question was: What was a sent organizational unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic's point is that the word "sent" may not relate to an organizational unit but just a unit. That's a question of interpretation of the document, Mr. Hannis. What we're looking for, Mr. Adamovic, is an example if you can think of one of a sent organizational unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An organizational unit cannot be sent. Let me just explain this to you. In the seat of the ministry there are organizational units called administrations and they exist within all police specialty affairs. And outside of those organizational units there are also branch organizational units, as we used to call them, or in other words units that exist outside of the seat of the ministry. Those units are called secretariats of the interior, and in Serbia there were a total of 33 secretariats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
