utterances.text: We understand all that. But in that case give us an example, please, of a sent unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say secretariats let me just say that all kinds of police work is performed within a secretariat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just deal with my question. Give me an example of a sent unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 35th Detachment of PJP, but that's not an organizational unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it may not matter, Mr. Hannis, whether it's an organizational unit or a unit. If it's a sent unit and it's under the auspices of the staff, does it matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, but I had an indication that perhaps there's some error in the translation in the document and maybe I need to ask the witness to read out item number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, could you read out item number 2 and we'll see if the translation we hear now is the same that's written in my English version.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The task of the staff is to plan, organize, and direct the work and engagement of organizational units of the ministry as well as sent and attached units aimed at suppressing terrorism in the territory of autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That clears it up a little bit for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it makes Mr. Lukic's point, I think. We shall require CLSS to revise the translation of paragraph 2, and I think we should have the whole of paragraph 2 revised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: While we're there --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not a CLSS translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh. Who translated this, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my understanding of how these were done, this looks like a CLSS translation, but I stand to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Even if it's not, that would be even better reason for having it done now. So we shall require it to be done. Mr. Hannis, you should remit this document to CLSS to translate paragraph 2 of the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And while we're hear, Colonel, could I just have you read the next sentence then in case there's something I want to ask you about that while we're here.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In addition to that, the staff has a task also to plan, organize, direct, and combine the work of organizational units of the ministry in Kosovo and Metohija in carrying out more complex special security tasks."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. With regard to paragraph 16 in your statement and planning I would like to show you Exhibit P3130. This is a -- these are conclusions from a meeting of secretariat chiefs and police detachment commanders from a meeting on the 2nd of November, 1998. And I'd like to go to item number 10, I think it's page 3 of the English and it's the last page in the B/C/S, I think it's the fourth page in the B/C/S -- I'm sorry, it's page 3 of the English. Can you see item number 10 on your screen? It says: "The MUP staff in Pristina will now take on the role of planning and the secretariats will have greater independence in carrying out their regular duties ..." Were you aware of this meeting and this conclusion that came out of it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I attended this meeting is something you can see in the minutes. I truly don't remember it myself. As for the conclusions, since I attended the meeting, whether I read them out there at the meeting or not, I really don't remember that. I suppose that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, do you know how things changed from November 1998 in terms of the MUP staff taking on the role of planning from the secretariats?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This formulation is not clear to me. I don't know what planning they have in mind because it says here that secretariats have greater autonomy in carrying out regular tasks. So based on that I can't conclude on the basis of what the analyst formulated this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just to orient you in time this meeting would have been about a week or ten days after the October Agreements were signed, you know, after discussions between Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Holbrooke and General Clark and General Naumann came and the OSCE-KVM mission was set up. Do you recall -- look at item number 8 and it talks about: "In villages with Serbian inhabitants, taking additional protection measures ..." And the next sentence says: "Make sure that Serbs and members of the reserve police squads don't misuse weapons," that they don't carry weapons or show them in public in the presence of members of the mission. And skipping one more sentence: "Tell them not to state the fact that Serbs are armed and to explain this fact, if they must, using the excuse that it's only members of the guard who are armed." Did you know of this conclusion in this effort to keep the mission from knowing about the arming of Serbs in Kosovo? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know about that because the contact was a daily one and members of the mission were present throughout the territory of Kosovo, and they had contact with secretariats, OUPs, and police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me move to a different item. You mention in paragraph 17 about being informed about the adoption of the plan to fight terrorism. If you would have a look at Exhibit 6D798. I'll hand you a copy -- I can hand you a hard copy if you don't have it. You'll see this is from a meeting at the Pristina MUP on the 22nd of July, 1998, and I seem to recall you said you were at this meeting -- yeah, I see your name in the list of those present. Item number 3 on the agenda is: "Defining tasks in the implementation of the Global Plan ..." Is this where you first heard about the plan to fight terrorism, at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you see that General Djordjevic, General Stevanovic, and General Lukic are all there. I understand from other evidence in this case that there had been a meeting in Belgrade a couple of days earlier where they -- those generals learned about this plan. Is that consistent with what you knew about it or what you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information. When the generals arrived, Generals Stevanovic and Djordjevic, we were informed to the extent necessary that such a plan had been adopted and that it was to be implemented by the police and the army. It was the plan for carrying out anti-terrorist actions, and that it was adopted at the level of the president of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. That was my next question. This document seems to end sort of in the middle. Three of the SUP chiefs speak and then there's nothing further. Do you know why this document appears to be incomplete? If you can look on the back of that page you will see it ends after the Prizren SUP chief speaks and there's nothing further.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear that it is incomplete, but I don't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who normally took the minutes of those meetings?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was down there it was mostly Desimir Slovic, who was also an analyst.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. In paragraph 18 of your statement you mention seeing a VJ document, Exhibit P2808, which is dated the 16th of February, 1999, that talks about propose anti-terrorist actions in the same areas that are set forth in the document 6D716 that you I think looked at earlier which is dated the 19th of February, 1999, and on the heading it says "MUP command." Do you remember looking at both those documents?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think when you were on direct testimony Mr. Ivetic asked you about that term "MUP command," you told us and you tell us in your statement that as far as you know there was never any body, any group or any body called the MUP command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that I spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In your statement you say, in paragraph 18: "A body called the MUP command has never existed ..."

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, all right, we did not understand each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we look at Exhibit P1613. You refer to this in your statement. I don't know if you have a copy of it there. I think Mr. Ivetic showed you a copy. If you don't have it, I can give you one.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this is a document that is titled "MUP command." It has a strictly confidential number 880-207 and it's dated 27th August 1998 and we see that it's signed by General Pavkovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this action called for in the Dobrodeljane sector involves the 549th Motorised Brigade supporting the 10th MUP Squad or I'm not sure if that's a correct pronunciation, and also the 1/9th MUP OD. Do you see that in item number 5.1?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know why the VJ General Pavkovic would be using the term "MUP command" in an order in August 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain that. All I know is that the term MUP command is something that I have never heard us use for as long as I've been in service.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you if in 1998 or 1999 while you were in Kosovo if you ever saw or heard the term Joint Command or Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999 while I was in Kosovo I did not see such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You never saw a document with the word "Joint Command" on it; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you never heard the term used by anybody in 1998 or 1999 in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the term, I did hear about it but I never saw a document using that term.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Tell us when and how you heard of the term Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's hard for me to pin-point the time. Even if I heard the term and when I heard the term, that term didn't have any particular meaning to me within my work at the staff nor in my contacts. I know that I contacted the Pristina Corps. So this is the term that had no weight as far as I was concerned and I wasn't interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, if you can't pin-point the time can you pin-point the circumstances, where you were and who you heard saying it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to answer that question. It is possible that I heard it when I went to visit people at the Pristina Corps, but I can't claim with any certainty from whom I heard that term.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I was a little confused yesterday when Mr. Ackerman was asking you about your involvement in conveying the VJ maps, map extracts, regarding joint actions. That's work that you did not only during the few days of the war while you were there, but you also did that in -- earlier in 1999 and in 1998, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Perhaps I wasn't focused.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite catch your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. The work you did in -- with Colonel Djakovic, you told us was your main contact at the VJ. In receiving maps and map extracts regarding joint anti-terrorist actions which you then passed along to the MUP units that were going to be involved, you did that not only in 1999 during the war before you got injured, but you also did it earlier in 1999 and in 1998, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that the only thing you received from the VJ were extracts or maps and map extracts; you didn't have any orders, any textual orders?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received extracts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And no textual orders? You'll have to answer out loud.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the textual part, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing whether any of those map extracts had the word "Joint Command" on them?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall having seen that. I remember that in the left corner it said either who approved this or whatever, and in the right one there was again somebody's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to follow the trial of Mr. Milosevic that took place here and the Kosovo portion of that trial? Did you read about it or watch it on TV?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not follow that trial at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about this trial, before coming here today did you read about it or watch any of it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't been following this trial either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Before coming to testify did you have any conversation with Colonel Mijatovic or Colonel Vucurevic or any of your former colleagues from the MUP staff in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Colonel Mijatovic only once. As for Mr. Vucurevic, I never saw him, never spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did -- and did you have a chance to read General Lukic's interview that he gave to the OTP investigators in May of 2002? Did you see that before coming to testify?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So is your evidence that you were not aware that the issue of the existence or not of a Joint Command in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and 1999 is something that's been a strongly contested issue in this case? You didn't know about that? Nobody told you that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that during the preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We've had some evidence in this case indicating that General Lukic attended more than 50-some meetings of the Joint Command in Kosovo in 1998 between July 22nd and the end of October of 1998. Were you not aware that your boss was going to Joint Command meetings two or three times a week, on average?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that General Lukic went to some meetings. Now, what meetings these were and what their content was, that's not something I asked him about and he did not talk to me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know who he was meeting with?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the information I have is -- well, again I'm saying as far as I know, that he went to some meetings. Was it to the Pristina Corps or wherever, I don't know, where there were representatives of the army and - if I can put it that way - representatives of some other state organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you weren't aware that David Gajic from the DB was also attending Joint Command meetings in Pristina in July and August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to your job of forwarding the maps and excerpts to MUP from the VJ, when did you first start doing that job? Was that shortly after you arrived in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was certainly after the 22nd after that meeting that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall who assigned you to do that task?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the head of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did General Lukic tell you why you were chosen for that job?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, he didn't. There was no need for him to explain to me why he had chosen me because there weren't that many of us on the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What instructions did he give you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To go from time to time to Colonel Djakovic and to submit information about the units that were in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, all with a view to planning the implementation of anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you've told us I think that your primary contact in the VJ was Colonel Djakovic, but you mention a second individual and I can't recall his name now. Who else from the VJ did you sometimes deal with on this matter?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, I think that his rank was that of lieutenant-colonel, it was Lieutenant-Colonel Tesevic, they were in the same area, in the same office, so I would see him there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you the only guy from MUP who was doing this job?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say for sure whether somebody else perhaps went sometimes. Sometimes I would go home to see my family, so I cannot say whether in the meantime it was necessary for someone else to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. But between late July 1999 and March 29th -- late July 1998 and March 29th, 1999, when you left, during the time you were at work this was your job and nobody else was doing it, right? You were the one who was picking up those map and map extracts and passing them on?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you keep any kind of a log or record book of what you received and passed on?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, records were not kept with regard to that matter, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So there was no tracking system in case something got lost, there was no way to go back and see when you had received it and when you had passed it off; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, really, we did not keep any records of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One of the questions I think Mr. Ackerman asked you and that I'm curious about too is if the Pristina Corps -- if the VJ is writing these orders and drawing up these maps for these joint actions, how did they know which MUP units to put in the map and the extract? How did they know what PJP detachment or whether the SAJ was available or whether it was going to be some PJP company from Pristina? How did the VJ get that information to incorporate in their plans and their maps?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was precisely my task to submit that kind of information. My first contact with Djakovic had to do with me having already given information about the units that were in the field on the detachments, since the detachments were mostly in the same locations. So Colonel Djakovic was kept abreast, and in a specific action I would just go to confirm whether it was that detachment, or rather, if the Pristina Corps had planned on more forces, then we would see who else could become involved as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you say that you kept no record or log-book, did you keep a copy of the extract map which you had passed on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not copies either. From the Pristina Corps we got excerpts from maps in an envelope for the units that were supposed to take part in that activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And did you open the envelope?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no need for that because we were not involved in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So how did you know to whom to deliver what was in the envelope?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the envelope it says who the envelope was supposed to go to, what unit, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So was there a separate envelope with a separate map for each MUP unit that was going to be engaged in an action? Is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is a broader action, then the unit would only get an excerpt for its own area, the area that it is supposed to take part in, because the map as a whole is bigger and several units are involved in the action. So a unit only gets its own excerpt for its own part.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, for example -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On you go, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For example, we've seen some VJ or Joint Command orders for rather large actions or operations that sometimes involved many units of both VJ and MUP. I don't have one right at hand, but some that would involve perhaps ten or more separate MUP units. And are you saying that there would be ten separate envelopes for each of those ten separate units regarding that one action and MUP did not receive an overall map showing where all its units were going to be involved, you only got ten separate little extracts. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would only get excerpts for the units that took part in the action. I think that in practice there weren't that many units involved, but I don't know the exact number. There were those involving larger and smaller number of participants.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you pursuing that? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm going to a related area, but if you want to touch on that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. You will remember yesterday we saw one of these maps with little markings on the map which were said to be ways of identifying the location of any unit at any time. If the MUP staff didn't have a copy of the map how would you know when reference was made to these numbers and indications on the map the location of the particular units of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These maps probably pertained to the time when I was not down there. While I was there, there were no such maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, we've heard evidence that one important function of the MUP staff was to provide emergency assistance when required, and identifying where that assistance might be required seemed to be of some importance. How would you be able to do that if you didn't have a copy of the map being used in the particular action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the staff did not participate in these activities regarding the implementation of actions. It is correct that at the time when actions were being implemented out in the field General Djordjevic was usually there or Obrad Stevanovic, both of them or one of the two. Now, what it was that they were doing there is something that I'm really not aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And regarding General Stevanovic and General Djordjevic, what way would they have of knowing where the various MUP units were deployed in these joint actions or would they have any way of knowing?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I can put it this way, they did not have to report to me how it was that they received their knowledge about all of this. I really do not know who they were in contact with. That is to say that that is beyond me since these are higher-ranking officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let me read you something that Colonel Mijatovic said when he was here and I'll ask you if that is correct. This is from the transcript at page 22441 through 442, and he said: "Depending on the area in which an anti-terrorist activity was being carried out, he," and he was referring to you, Adamovic, "provided information as to which MUP units were in the area so they might be reckoned with and become part of the plan. There was no need to take any decisions. There was no special need to have any decisions because the unit was there, was in the area, and the unit would now be involved." And then I asked him: "Well, did it work then that the VJ first told Adamovic, I need 300 men? And Adamovic said, These 300 are available. Is that how it worked?" And he said: "In principle, yes. They didn't say later on it has to be this or that detachment, but they said Dusko Adamovic says we can have this or that unit in the area that can get involved, and they," meaning the army, "can go on with planning." And I asked him if that's how it worked in reality and he said: "Yes." Is that correct, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the essence is that when I went to the Pristina Corps that I gave information about the units that were in the area and that could take part in activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How did that work when you went to the Pristina Corps? Did they show you on the map where they were planning to engage in some activity and you had -- you had some map or some book of your own where you could look and say, Oh, the 37th Detachment is right there, you can use them? How did it work or did you know in your head where everybody was? How did that work?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I'd come to the corps the map was already there, or rather, the map was already being worked on, so I knew where the units were since there weren't that many locations there. So already in advance I know where it is that these units are, I mean in global terms the area where they are. And then the Pristina Corps would continue its activities in terms of rounding off this job, if I can put it that way, and then when I come again the map excerpt had already been made and forwarded further.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I've seen in some of the orders that there's maybe a pretty small MUP contingent tasked for a job, for example, a company, maybe a company. How would the VJ know which company of a particular detachment was available for the job? You might have three or four companies in a detachment, right, and how would the VJ know which one was taking a rest or depleted from the previous action, et cetera? Do you understand that question?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand you. I never gave information about a specific company from a specific detachment. The only thing that could happen was that within the implementation of certain actions the Pristina Corps would suggest that a company be involved of the 124th Intervention Brigade; and in every secretariat there was one respectively except for Pristina where there were two. So these were the companies, but Colonel Djakovic knew that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, is this an appropriate time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is. This has been a lengthy cross-examination because of the questions to be asked by other counsel. Some of that must have been of assistance to you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It was, Your Honour, and I've tried to eliminate the matters that Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cepic covered that were originally on my list, but I still have substantial amount of materials I think this witness is in the best position to help --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you to get to the end today?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm going to do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Adamovic, we need another break at this stage for half an hour. Could you again leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, I'd like to show you an exhibit and I don't think you have a copy, I'll give you a hard copy of this one, this is P1428, it's a Pristina Corps command decision from the 14th of August, 1998, on breaking up Siptar terrorists in the Slup and Voksa villages sector. You'll see under item number 1 -- I'm sorry, item number 2, point 1 on the first page, task for units, the battle group 15-3 is to support the attack of the 8th MUP Detachment in the Djakovica PJP company. How would -- how would the VJ know about the availability of the Djakovica PJP company to assist in an action like this? Would that information come from you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the carrying out of actions, officers of the police and the army out in the field had daily contact and in this particular case when it comes to the 8th Detachment and the Djakovica PJP company it is certain that the military commanders received documents via their own chain, documents pertaining to the action, because they took part in the action just like the police units did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. But I think that's true for all the joint actions, correct? All the joint --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the joint ones. The Army of Yugoslavia would receive it down their own chain of command and then the police would receive it as I have explained to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well -- so how would the VJ know to send through you an excerpt map to the Djakovica PJP company? Wouldn't they have had to receive information from you beforehand that that company was available for the planned action?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, prior to that I gave information to the Pristina Corps and then the documents were drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You don't remember this one specifically, do you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, I really don't, since I didn't take part in the planning, not in a single segment of it except for what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you would go to the last page and it's page 3 of the English and the last page in B/C/S, item number 6 is command and communications. It says: "Combat operations will be commanded by the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija." I take it from your earlier answer then that you never saw this document in 1998 where it has a reference to the Joint Command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on the last page we see this order signed by Colonel Vladimir Lazarevic, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me give you another -- a related document from August 1998, with the help of the usher I'll trade you. This is Exhibit P1427 from a few days earlier, the 10th of August, 1998, signed on the last page, you'll see this one's signed by General Pavkovic. It's a decision on the joint engagement of MUP and VJ forces, and item number 2.1 and 2.2 make reference to the SAJ. Did you also have the knowledge and information about where SAJ units were located for making determinations about what MUP units were available to assist in areas where actions were planned by the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what was your source of that information? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SAJ, just like the police detachments, was sent to Kosovo and Metohija in order to carry out anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that, but how did you know where they were? Did you get that information from Colonel Trajkovic or where did you get that information from?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The movement of units was monitored.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: By whom? By you personally?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since planned actions were carried out, it was known which unit takes part in which action. Normally when an action was over or after some time another one would start, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, but on a day or a couple days before August 10th, when this decision was made for this action to include SAJ units, how did you know where the SAJ was in order to be able to advise the VJ that the SAJ is in that area and you could use them ? How would you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was known where the SAJ was stationed whenever it was not involved in an action. Just like all other units, once they complete a task in a certain area, they withdraw, if we may call it that, to the location where they were before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you say it was known. My question is: How did you know that? Did you receive a daily report? Where were you getting that information from and able to -- in order to be able to tell the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have a specific information and I didn't need it. This activity was underway from the 25th of July and it went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So when this activity began on the 25th of July, I take it you know where the SAJ was; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And between the 25th of July and the 10th of August, I gather that they participated in some other actions. How did you know where they were between the 25th of July and the 10th of August? You must have received some sort of updated information from someone.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Updated information was not needed. I'm not saying that from time to time certain officers wouldn't stop by the staff or establish some sort of contact, but if the SAJ was stationed in Pristina, say when not involved in an action, whenever the action was over say in Podujevo or elsewhere, they would go back to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So are you saying then that immediately before the 10th of August they were in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't claim for this specific case that they were in Pristina, I can't remember, but there were cases when actions continued. So I'm not claiming that they were in Pristina on that particular occasion, I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So if they were not in Pristina, how would you find out where they actually were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They could have been either in their base or out there performing an action. If they were carrying out a planned action, then it was known where they were; that is to say they did not have some other tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And if they were carrying out a planned action, how was it known that they would be available for this action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Pristina Corps kept track of actions underway, both because of the police forces and the army forces because those forces could not be at two different places at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So in the end of the day you're saying that your input into identifying the location and availability of the SAJ was zero?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I said. I repeat, they were located in Kosovo and Metohija and they had been sent there in order to carry out anti-terrorist actions. If, for example, at the Pristina Corps it was requested that the SAJ should participate, then they would, and in that case I would provide information and in that case in the Pristina Corps they would include them in their plans just like all other units participating in any other action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what is the information that you would provide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would provide information only about units which were located in a certain area, that is to say that I did not propose that, for example, SAJ should be sent to Pec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand. So you would tell the Colonel Djakovic where particular parts of the SAJ were? Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How did you find out where they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew that they were either out there performing a task or they were in their base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I ask you the question again: How did you find out where they were? Just please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once an activity was over in a certain area the secretariats would inform the staff or sometimes it happened that officers of -- from the units would occasionally contact, make contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's taken us five minutes to get to that and that's the question you were asked by Mr. Hannis. Please try to answer the questions you're being asked. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I lost my place. I think that was my last question about that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you look on the last page and tell us to whom that document was sent. Well, let me speed it up. The second one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just give us a moment, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, I would tell you that item number 6 of this one also indicates that combat operations will be commanded by the Joint Command, and it's sent to -- at the very end you'll see it's sent to the Pristina Corps command and to the Republic of Serbia MUP PJP command. Do you know who that would be in August 1998? Who would be the PJP command?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that the command of the PJP of the MUP of Serbia did not exist in Kosovo. I see that this document was drafted in Djakovica. I had no occasion to see it before and it would be difficult for me to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you if you were at the MUP staff and this document came in from the VJ addressed to the MUP PJP command, who would you pass it on to?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a difficult question. The command of the PJP of the MUP was envisioned once the -- once PJP units of the MUP were planned. So it existed in plans as a command, but it was never made operational, it never started functioning. At one point in time there existed also a commander of the PJP; that's why it's difficult for me to give you a -- an opinion as to whether they planned to deliver this to somebody and when and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you were a member of the MUP staff in Kosovo in 1998 and you were involved in sort of passing on orders or decision maps regarding joint actions involving PJP. There must be somebody that you would have gone to see about this. Who was the highest-ranking person in Kosovo dealing with PJP in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that there was a specific person in Kosovo that was in charge of dealing with the PJP. I told you what -- who the people were who were located in Kosovo, both members of the staff and those who were not. When it comes to this logistical support we, people from the staff, got involved in it. And when there were events taking place on the ground, I don't have full information as to how that transpired.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me read you something from the OTP interview of General Lukic related to this question. This is Exhibit P948. This is the combined B/C/S, English version of that interview at page 53, and the preceding question from the investigator to General Lukic was: "Were you controlling the PJP?" And he said: "All police units which were there had a primary role, primary task, which was curbing terrorism. The task of the staff, the headquarters, was to coordinate the work of these units." Would you agree with that, was that the task of the MUP staff to coordinate the work of those units combatting terrorism?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that would be an appropriate term to describe what the staff did, if we take into account all the things that we enumerated, all the things that the staff did then one could say that this is correct, that that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that's consistent with part of item number 2 in Exhibit P1505, that order or decision establishing a MUP staff to combat terrorism, 16 June 1998, right? That talked about one of the things the staff was to do was to coordinate those units in complex security actions, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't coordinate that activity in that manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me continue on with this answer. General Lukic says: "And speaking of this, the special police units, PJP, had dual responsibility, one was to the commander of the PJP units and the other one was to the Chief of Staff." And the investigator said: "And who had primacy over what they did, was it something that you," General Lukic, "you had to agree together or was Stevanovic able to instruct them or were you able to instruct them?" And the answer was: "As of mid-July," this is 1998, "until the end of September, beginning of October that year, I was in more or less permanent company of Mr. Djordjevic and Mr. Stevanovic, they were always with me, in the hierarchy structure they are by all means above the Chief of Staff because they are ministers. That is why I say that they had parallel responsibility in performing their task." Would you agree with General Lukic in that description about his role and General Stevanovic's role vis-a-vis the PJP in 1998? Would you agree or would you disagree?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't listen to this attentively all the way until the end, but let me say this: Generals Stevanovic and Djordjevic were both in Kosovo, and as I have told you, they would frequently go to locations where the units were. We from the staff were less on the move, if I may say so, were less mobile or we didn't really go out in the field or we went seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The transcript is on the screen in front of you in both English and B/C/S. Did you not understand my question was: Did you agree with General Lukic where he's saying in essence that the PJP had dual responsibility, one was to the commander of the PJP units and the other was to the Chief of Staff? And I take that to mean Stevanovic and Lukic. Would you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you have in mind when you say "Chief of Staff"? Because to my knowledge we did not have a Chief of Staff. When it comes to PJP units it is true that commanders of detachments were responsible for the tasks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, Mr. Hannis put his question on the basis that that is a reference to General Lukic. Just accept that for the moment. We'll determine in due course whether it is. Accepting that, do you agree with the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can just read this. It's hard for me to formulate this. At any rate, Obrad Stevanovic covered PJP units or in other words, he was the commander of PJP units until 1997, and it is certain that he did have contact with officers on the ground, more so than General Lukic who was in the staff in Pristina. I hope that this answer is to your satisfaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it's not to my satisfaction. I asked you if you agreed or disagreed. Can you not answer it or do you just not want to answer it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not whether I want to or do not want to. Can you please put shorter questions to me so that I can give you very specific answers because I presented to you the essence. So it's difficult for me to answer in this manner. When it comes to hierarchy, now that I'm looking at this text, in the sense of hierarchy they are above the head of staff given the roles that they have, chief of the sector and assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you one that may be easier. Would you agree that General Lukic in 1998 was in a better position than you to know what his relationship as Chief of Staff or head of the MUP staff with the PJP was?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is only natural that he knows better what it was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Before we leave this document, P1427, I have one last question. Item 2.1 and 2.2 make reference to the 2nd MUP Detachment and the 9th MUP Detachment. You told us how the units that came from Serbia which had, for example, two-digit designators, when they came to Kosovo in 1998 Colonel Djakovic sort of re-assigned them designators and they got digits 1 through 10. And as I understand, you and Colonel Djakovic knew the code or the key as to which one was which. Is that right so far?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you remember now what was the designator for the 2nd MUP Detachment in Kosovo? What was its two-digit designator in Serbia proper outside of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Detachment I think that was the 36th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the 9th, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 9th I think was the 37th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that written down in a document somewhere that you had?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know whether I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me go back to your work in passing along the VJ orders to MUP units. Colonel Mijatovic told us that in late April 1999 - and I'm reading from the transcript at page 22196 - he said: "After the order on subordination was received, in addition to these excerpts from maps we got the textual part of the task in the form of orders." I guess you were gone by then, so you wouldn't have seen any of those; is that right? You were gone from Kosovo by late April 1999, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left at the end of March, yes, yes, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And Colonel Zivaljevic was here and testified about how he received maps, and he said there were a couple of ways. From the transcript page 24903 he said: "When the conditions allowed I would stop by the Pristina staff, they would prepare in envelopes documents for me, and this is how I would take those documents sometimes. And sometimes when I wasn't able to go I would send a courier and the courier would go and bring back the envelope that was intended for me." And he said that you were the one who distributed documents. Is that right, do you recall distributing some of these map or map excerpts to Colonel Zivaljevic in person and by courier?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say anything specific about Colonel Zivaljevic, but in principle I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And Colonel Mijatovic told us regarding the maps that were received from the VJ at page 22196, he said: "In 1998 for every anti-terrorist action that had been planned the staff received excerpts from maps where there were markings." Now, I understood your earlier answer to say that you received these things already in the envelopes. How would Colonel Mijatovic know that there were markings on the map if you just got envelopes with the maps inside?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I went to the Pristina Corps and when I took the maps of course I saw them during the preparation while they were working on them, and primarily it was the excerpt and it said what unit this related to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So then you went back to MUP and you prepared envelopes with the addressee MUP units on them and put the maps inside the envelopes; is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, already on the envelopes it was written what unit this related to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And that was done at the VJ, at the Pristina Corps command? You will have to answer out loud.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you write those addresses on the envelope or did Djakovic or somebody from the VJ do it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was already written who it was for, for what unit I mean, not on an individual basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You said when Mr. Ackerman was asking you some questions, he tried to suggest that in your passing on these orders that you were in essence ordering subordinate units of the MUP. And you said at page 24974 you said: "It cannot be put that way. I was not issuing orders. The basis for police action was the plan that had been adopted for carrying out anti-terrorist actions." Now, you're referring to the global plan that we saw referred to in that 22 July meeting; is that the basis?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that plan was the basis for carrying out anti-terrorist actions and I did not issue any other orders or instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see a written version of that plan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that the answer was not finished because the answer was: And other orders and instructions were not issued by me. So -- and it can be checked on the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We would like a revised translation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Perhaps the witness can repeat his answer because he did trail off at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but it's much more important that we get the spontaneous original answer so we will ask for a revised translation of page 82, 4 and 5. Please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At page 24979 Mr. Ackerman suggested that you were basically a post office box in your description of how you were passing these on, and you said: "I explained how I established contacts and what it was that I told Colonel Djakovic. The outlines of the maps would most frequently be done before my arrival." I wasn't clear on what you -- what it was that you told Djakovic. Are you referring to giving him information about what MUP units were available in particular areas? Is that what you meant there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the units that were in these areas, of course before being involved in that particular task so that he could involve them in his plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You said, also to Mr. Ackerman I think, in discussing that exhibit, P1505, the decision to establish a MUP staff for suppression of terrorism and item number 2 about planning and organizing and managing the activities and use of organizational units you said: "The reality looked differently." How was the reality different in Kosovo in 1998 from what's described in that exhibit we looked at earlier?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as organizational units are concerned of the ministry, or rather, the secretariats that were in Kosovo, if I can put it this way they retained all their functions and carried out all their other tasks like other secretariats, like fighting crime and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Related to that, Mr. Ackerman asked you about: "Why would the minister order these kinds of things that were contained in paragraph 2 and 3 of that decision if he didn't mean it?" And you said: "It was difficult to comment. And if we compare that with the practice it's obvious that these tasks are not good." Why were these tasks not good? What was the problem with these tasks listed in paragraph 2 and 3 of this exhibit? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't understand that the minister put in that document the obligation of the staff to organize and plan and direct the work of the secretariats. I don't know what he meant, how the staff could do that, take over the role of the secretariats. Would that be it? I mean, that would not be possible. The staff did not have the capacity to take over the directing of these secretariats and that they would be some kind of organizational unit of the staff and when we know that the staff was not an organizational unit in its own right so it is hard for me to understand that, at least for me it's hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you said that before, that there seemed to be a problem with shortage of staff to do what's described here, but in this document right above item number 2 it says: "Other members of the ministry may be appointed to the staff on the request of the head of staff." Did you or other members of the staff suggest to General Lukic that he should request more staff and order to carry out the task contemplated for MUP staff? You didn't do that, did you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that we talked about that and that that was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I think you were asked a couple questions about the reserve police stations. You were aware of the creation of those things in Kosovo in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about the creation, but I did not work on that, another officer did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that Captain Pesic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think there was somebody else sent down from Belgrade to assist on that. Was there a Colonel Stanojevic or ...

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was down there, he was not a colonel, and -- he was a general, rather, General Momcilo Stojanovic, but as far as I know he was sent on some other assignments, of course apart from the staff, not in the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You're not aware of him assisting with matters regarding the reserve police stations?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what he was assisting with and his role was not fully clear, to me at least, because he dealt with the procurement of apartments, not the actual allocation of apartments but procurement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me hand you another document, this is Exhibit P3121. These are the minutes of a meeting on the 28th of July at the MUP in Pristina, and Minister Stojiljkovic attended along with the head of his office, General Markovic, General Lukic, and other members of the staff, I see you're listed here. I think you told us you recall attending this meeting and as a matter of fact you were listed as speaking on page 4 of the English, I think it's page 4 in the B/C/S. Mr. Cepic asked you some of these questions about the armoured vehicles, et cetera. I have a question for you on that. You say: "We equipped police units with infantry weapons and weapons systems." What kind of weapons were you talking about there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about small arms, as we called them, these are smaller calibres up to 7.9 millimetres, if it can be put that way and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay -- I'm sorry, did you have something else to say?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And when referring to artillery pieces then it's the mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you could go to page 8 in your B/C/S, it's page 7 of the English, and if you could find for me, Colonel, about a little bit more than half way down Captain Pesic is speaking at this meeting. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He says: "We formed 243 reserve police stations. Weapons have been issued to 54.683 persons, MUP issued some 12.000, Yugoslav Army issued weapons to 34.000, and when all of this is finished about 60.000 persons will have been issued weapons." Do you remember that being discussed at this meeting, you were aware of the arming of these reserve police stations and individuals?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember whether this was mentioned at that meeting, but obviously this activity lasted --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you repeat the end of your answer there, please, Mr. Adamovic, it was not picked up by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that it was obvious that this activity had taken place earlier on as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could read at the very bottom of your page, and it's on page 8 of the English, where General Lukic is speaking he says: "We are arming citizens in towns and plans for defending towns have been drawn up. Chiefs of secretariats have the duty to organize the defence of towns in agreement with the Yugoslav Army, reserve police stations, and other bodies." Did you have any knowledge of or role in drawing up these plans for defending towns?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where General Lukic says that the chiefs of the secretariats have a duty to organize defence and agreement with the army reserve police stations and other bodies, do you know what the other bodies refers to there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If what is meant here are plans that were made, that are made, defence plans as we call them, then what is envisaged are possible situations and, if we can put it that way, forces that are required. These are the so-called war plans that are made in all the secretariats and at all levels. That's how it was done, if I can put it that way, in the days of the former Yugoslavia and obviously it went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not sure you answered my question, though. Do you know what other bodies he was referring to? We've heard talk about civil protection, civil defence, we've seen a reference to some -- we've seen a reference in some VJ combat orders to armed non-Siptar population. Do you know what he's referring to here when he says "other bodies"?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- other structures. I don't understand, unless it's the local self government. I don't know. I wouldn't want to guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Other structures are obviously some organs, not individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know I said I would do my best to finish by 7.00, but I think I have about 20 minutes more after 7.00. It's taken me longer to get some answers than I anticipated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, see what you can do in your five minutes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we'll look at the position tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on the last page of that document, Colonel, Mr. Cepic asked you about the remark of Minister Stojiljkovic about commanding is better. I want you to pick up from there. It says: "Lieutenant-General Rade Markovic will be in Prizren to help." In this time-period, July 1998, do you know what General Rade Markovic's position was in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Had he already replaced Mr. Stanisic that early? I thought that didn't take place until later.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say for sure. I think that he had already become that by then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was the position he held before he was chief of the state security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I remember correctly, I think he came from the position of the chief of the secretariat in Belgrade, I think that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then Minister Stojiljkovic goes on to say: "You should plan activities of the PJP in advance with chiefs of SUPs and hold a meeting on this." Who is he addressing there? He must be addressing you on the MUP staff, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's addressing all the attendees.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, apart from the minister and his head of office, General Markovic, General Lukic, we see you and other staff members and we see, I think, one, two, three, four SUP chiefs. So that must mean General Lukic and the rest of you on the staff, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And he says: "You should make somebody at the staff level responsible for dealing with discipline of police members." Who he's talking to there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously the staff or the head of staff or -- he's addressing everyone, but this seems to show that it's the staff that's supposed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And after this meeting in July 1998 do you know what steps were taken to have somebody at the staff level responsible for the discipline of police officers or police members?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know which one of us was in charge of that specifically. At any rate, I know that at all meetings that were organized at the staff this was discussed and orders were issued as far as discipline was concerned, professionalism, lawfulness on the part of the members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And Judge Bonomy asked you earlier about did you possibly consider yourself to be number two in the staff under General Lukic. And you said you could not consider yourself number two because you knew who number two was. Who was number two during the time you were there in your view?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for number two, at that time there wasn't one since Mijatovic came a few days after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So is he the one you considered number two during the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't pay attention to these ten days or whatever, so I considered Mijatovic to be this number two. That is why there was this slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, is this an appropriate time to break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It would be if I understood that answer. Perhaps someone will clarify it later, but it's -- you would expect from the previous answer that the question you asked would get a one-word answer, Mr. Hannis but --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hopes exist simply to be dashed. All right. We have to finish our session for the day at this stage. Mr. Adamovic, I'm afraid you'll have to return again tomorrow to hopefully complete your evidence at that stage; that will be in this courtroom at 2.15 tomorrow. Please again bear in mind what I said about lack of communication with anyone about the evidence in this case and return here ready to resume at 2.15 tomorrow. Now please leave the courtroom with the usher.
